🇲🇽🌡️ <u>CDMX DEPLOYS DATA LAB AGAINST EXTREME HEAT, PILOT IN IZTAPALAPA</u>

Mexico City's environment ministry (SEDEMA) and WRI Mexico launched the Cool Cities Lab to map heat risk with high-precision geographic data and turn it into prevention programs, with Iztapalapa as the pilot borough. "Extreme heat has become one of the main climate risks in Mexico City," said SEDEMA climate director Ana Mendívil. The city's Climate Action Program projects temperature increases above 2°C by mid-century.

🇲🇽♀️ <u>UN NAMES VIOLENCE AGAINST MOTHERS — MEXICO'S SEARCHING MOTHERS ARE IN THE REPORT</u>

A new UN report by Special Rapporteur Reem Alsalem recognizes violence and discrimination against mothers as a specific form of abuse — and explicitly names Mexico's madres buscadoras, women who face threats and harassment for searching for their disappeared children. The data behind it: women do 2.5 times more unpaid care work than men, 800 million lack economic security around childbirth, and 1 in 4 leave the labor market in their first year of motherhood.

🇲🇽📚 <u>MEXICO'S ANSWER TO SCREEN ADDICTION: PAUSE, THINK, READ</u>

At the president's morning press conference, education researcher Yarenia Analí Domínguez Delgado laid out the thinking behind Mexico's push for reading and phone limits in schools: "The challenge for our schools is not to compete with the speed of the screens." Her formula for the classroom: resistance, care and community — recovering attention and human bonds instead of delegating thinking to algorithms. "Learning doesn't always require more stimuli; sometimes it requires us to stop and think."

🇲🇽🌿 <u>CHIMALAPAS: 400 ZOQUE COMMUNEROS MOVE TO RECLAIM COMMUNAL LANDS</u>

On August 4, more than 400 comuneros of San Miguel Chimalapa, Oaxaca, acting on a mandate from their communal assembly, gathered at a boundary point with Chiapas — the ejido Gustavo Díaz Ordaz, a settlement of irregular origin administered by Chiapas but enclaved in zoque communal territory. Josefa Sánchez Contreras calls it one more action in the long struggle for communal lands — a conflict rooted in a 1967 presidential resolution the zoques say proves the land is theirs.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>PEMEX RAMPS UP DIESEL OUTPUT 42% AS MIDDLE EAST WAR DRIVES FUEL COSTS UP</u>

Energy sovereignty in action. Pemex produced an average of 270,000 barrels of diesel per day in the first half of 2026 — a 41.69% jump from the 190,000 bpd of a year earlier — while cutting diesel imports by 16.9%. Gasoline output rose 13.01% to 378,000 bpd. With global fuel prices spiking on the Middle East conflict, Mexico is refining more of its own instead of buying it abroad.

text: ‍FREIGHTWAVES: ANPACT warns tariffs threaten truck trade as exports surge August 16, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Straight trade coverage, no editorializing: Mexico's heavy-truck production jumped 51.8% in July, and 92.4% of its truck exports go to the US. 🇲🇽📈 <u>DELOITTE: MEXICO HEADED FOR HISTORIC EXPORT BOOM IN 2026</u>

Even the private sector's cautious voices concede it: Mexico is on track for a historic export boom this year, tariffs and all. Deloitte's Econosignal report shows high-value manufacturing surging — electronic components up 10.6% annually, aerospace up 16.2% — while it forecasts 1.2% GDP growth and notes national content in exports sits at 44%, stuck at 2015 levels. Fair warning, and exactly what Plan México's industrial policy is built to fix. The boom is real; the task now is to make it more Mexican.
